Alex — thanks for the logs, Alex and Camila. Quick engineering summary from the initial triage (01:20–08:30 PDT window):

Root cause (summary):
- A regression in our autoscaling router caused a small fraction (~8–14%) of the POC requests to be routed to a legacy hosted variant that had a slower quantization profile when sequence lengths exceeded 512 tokens.
- Concurrently, an internal batching policy did not apply prefix caching for these routed requests which magnified per-request latency.
- This combination produced high tail latency (p95–p99) and a 5xx spike because some older nodes hit a socket timeout under load.

What we pulled and attached:
- runtime-trace-0517.log (server-side traces for affected host IDs)
- latency-metrics-0517.csv (histograms and request IDs aligned with your sample)

Mitigation performed:
- We rolled back the autoscaler routing change at 02:10 PDT and added a temporary rule to force all POC traffic to the dedicated pool.
- We patched the batching policy to ensure prefix caching for the affected model family.

Proposed remedial offer (engineering + commercial recommendation):
- Apply a one-time service credit equal to 15% of the billed token usage for the window 01:20–08:30 PDT (estimated as 80k tokens).
- Add a 30-day trial extension to the existing POC (to make up for lost evaluation time).
- Priority support for the next 30 days with 1-hour response SLA for critical incidents.

I've attached the metrics and will coordinate a deeper postmortem with SRE; if that postmortem shows systemic issues beyond the routing regression we'll revisit the credit scale.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
